questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had heard really good things about Melbourne and its student life - and besides, it was important to me that it was an English-speaking country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The host university had sent out a guide to the students about important information etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As mentioned, the university had made a thorough guide with step by step for important things for arrival and the first few days. And if you needed help with something, you could meet at "stop1", which was located at the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The housing hunt was not super easy. We had been told that we could easily find housing on arrival - however, I would recommend searching from home, for example on Flatmates or Fairyfloss (Facebook pages). It is also clearly easier to find something alone rather than going with others.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is clearly best to find a room with some of the locals - there are many student accommodations, which actually also work super well. But you clearly get the most out of the experience if you find a private place to stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The entire registration process is sent out by e-mail - and there are simply different steps you have to follow, also in relation to important dates, e.g. with registration for subjects etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always get help from either KU or the host university - and as mentioned, there was "Stop 1" on arrival, where there was always someone who could help, regardless of whether it was about about your subjects, bupa or something like that.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Registering for the classes was super easy, and you could choose which times of the week you wanted the subjects - as long as you were aware of the dates for registering this.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of information and registration processes you just have to go through - but it is okay easy as long as you follow what is sent to you and pay attention to the dates.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: We had the opportunity to choose subjects between levels 1-3. It was very clear that level 1 was super easy and level 3 was more difficult. But in general, I would personally say that the level at home is higher - however, there is more work during the semester, as you are graded on all assignments, which end up in an overall grade.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching itself is very similar to the one we know at home with lectures and practice lessons.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Principles of Management, Marketing Communication, Performance, Potential and Development, Graphic Design

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Marketing Communication was super nice, we also had a really good teacher. Principle of Management was also very interesting (and easy).

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Wouldn't say there was anything unexpected, but just that Australia is a super expensive place to live, especially in terms of food and experiences

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The same as above regarding food and experiences

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university were super good at organizing events especially for exchange students, everything from cultural to sports events, you could simply follow along on various social media and see when and where different events took place

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely participate in the orientation week, as there are a lot of fun activities and plenty of opportunity to meet a lot of the other exchanges. In addition, I would recommend to join a club/sport - I participated in the surf club, which organized weekend trips and events occasionally

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Great Ocean Road, Surf trip to Torquay, extended weekend trip to Sydney, go to Byron Bay in mid-semester break, Mornington Peninsula, wine-tour to Yarra Valley etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Super easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Definitely become part of a sport/club or find a job, it's super easy and definitely the easiest way to meet the locals

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That Australians are the most open and welcoming people, so friendly and nice to be around

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Take advantage of the weekends and go on weekend trips, enjoy all of it (time flies:)), explore Melbourne, there are so many great places to see and experience

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go, you will never regret it. Melbourne is the most amazing city

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The whole experience - getting the opportunity to live in Australia, study at a super good university and meet so many different and nice people - as well as see and experience so many beautiful places

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Be on your own and create your own everyday life in a foreign country

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
